summary: No evidence of installer-side harm in diezyyasha-baileys@9.1.2
details: Package appears to be a fork or republish under the Baileys (WhatsApp Web library) name family. No a static rule matches and no traced install-time or import-time behavior indicating credential harvesting, exfiltration, remote code execution, silent-relay, dropper activity, or backdoor mechanisms were observed in the scanned content. The name resembles the widely-used Baileys library, which is a common vector for lookalike/typosquat packages, but name resemblance alone is not a supply-chain threat and the code content examined here does not exhibit an installer-harm mechanism.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
